_readme: Copy this file to providers.json (same folder) and fill in your keys.
providers.json is gitignored and never printed or logged by the tool.
Every preset speaks the OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions protocol.
Remote providers need a real api_key; local servers ignore the key but
the field must exist (use "none"). Set max_tokens generously: these are
reasoning-heavy calls and a small cap truncates the JSON replies.
Optional: "timeout" is the seconds allowed for one reply (default 1800),
"rate_limit_wait" the seconds to wait out a busy provider (default 900).
Test one with:  python -m worldgen check-provider <name>

zai._comment: z.ai API (https://z.ai/openplatform/api-docs). The model measured with this pipeline was glm-5.3-flash.

zai-coding._comment: z.ai coding-plan subscription (GLM coding plan), same API, different endpoint.

openrouter._comment: OpenRouter aggregates many providers; model ids look like vendor/name (see https://openrouter.ai/models).

ollama._comment: Ollama local server (https://ollama.com); run: OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 ollama serve. Key unused.

lmstudio._comment: LM Studio local server (Developer tab -> Start Server); model is whatever you loaded. Key unused.

llama-swap._comment: llama-swap proxies to locally configured models (https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap); model = a name from its config. Key unused unless you put one in front of it.
